task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 31, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper explainer answering why a 20% increase in a property's taxable assessment does not necessarily produce a 20% increase in its city property-tax bill.

facts.text: The city of Aldercove sent new property assessments in August 2026 alongside a council-approved reduction in its city tax rate.
The city rate falls from $1.50 to $1.30 per $100 of taxable assessed value for the next billing year.
A supplied city example increases a home's taxable assessment from $200,000 to $240,000, a 20% rise.
At the old value and rate, that home's city charge is $3,000; at the new value and rate, it is $3,120.
The example city charge therefore increases $120, or 4%, rather than 20%.
The figures concern taxable value after applicable adjustments, not an estimate of cash a homeowner has received.
County and school charges appear separately and are not included in the city's $3,000-to-$3,120 comparison.
Those other authorities have not all finalized their rates, so the example is not a complete forecast of the owner's combined property-tax bill.
Assessments estimate property values while the elected council sets the city rate through its budget process.
The city assessor says individual assessment changes vary; the 20% example is not the increase assigned to every property.
The city budget calls for a larger total levy despite the lower rate because the aggregate taxable base has grown.
Some base growth comes from newly completed buildings rather than solely from higher values on existing homes.
Homeowner Tera Moss said her wages did not rise when the assessed value of her house did.
Moss said, "The house may have a bigger number on paper, but I still pay the bill from the same paycheck."
Finance director Oren Fenn said, "The assessment and the rate are two parts of one multiplication, set through different decisions."
The city provides an account calculator using the adopted city rate but labels other authorities' unfinished charges as unavailable.
The assessor's notice explains a valuation-review process; that process does not itself change the council's adopted tax rate.
The reporting record provides no estimate of how many households will receive a lower combined bill.
Aldercove carries out a full assessment review every four years rather than valuing every property from a new sale each year.
No citywide rent increase, house-sale windfall or change in mortgage payments can be calculated from the supplied example alone.

forbidden_additions: Every property's bill rises 20% or the example forecasts the entire combined bill
A lower tax rate necessarily means a lower levy or cash income for homeowners
preserve: If quoted: The house may have a bigger number on paper, but I still pay the bill from the same paycheck.
If quoted: The assessment and the rate are two parts of one multiplication, set through different decisions.
The stated city charge rises from $3,000 to $3,120, a 4% increase.
